raw_response:
I'm 47 years old, been back in Quzhou County farming these 70 mu for 6 years now, after working construction in Shijiazhuang. Middle school education — I can read the extension pamphlets the county sends around, but honestly I learn more from watching my neighbors. My wife and I do most of the work. Our daughter is in high school and only helps on weekends, so I hire workers during the busy peaks.

The main part of my farm, 40 mu, is in wheat-maize double cropping. The wheat went in last October and is coming out of winter dormancy now. The stand looks okay — not the best I've had, but decent. Urea is running 2.6 yuan per kilo this year, up again. The extension fellow said I should topdress 15 kg N per mu at green-up, but for 40 mu that's a lot of cash all at once. I'm putting down 10 kg per mu now in early March, and if the wheat still looks yellow at jointing I'll add another 5 kg. Last year I did 12 kg topdress and got about 450 kg per mu, so I'm not going to push it. I also need to keep money aside for maize seed and fertilizer in June.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. That window is brutal — sometimes only five or six days between combine harvest and planting. I hire a custom combine and a planter; no way to do 40 mu by hand in that heat. I'll use hybrid seed, put down compound fertilizer at planting, and maybe a small urea topdress at the 10-leaf stage if rain is scarce.

Cotton is on 15 mu in the south field. It's heavy on labor, especially picking in September and October, but last year lint prices were decent at about 15 yuan per jin. I plant hybrid Bt cotton in late April, base fertilizer at planting, then topdress at flowering. Need to spray for bollworms — they were bad two years ago and wiped out my neighbor's yield.

Then there's my vegetable gamble: 5 mu watermelon by the well (good water access), 5 mu cauliflower as an early spring crop, and 5 mu chili. Cauliflower goes in now and comes off in May before wheat harvest, so the timing works. Watermelon and chili go in late April to early May. Vegetables pay better than grain when prices hold, but if they crash I'm stuck with produce I can't sell. I'm keeping the area small because I can't afford to lose big.

My material input budget is about 21,000 yuan this year. I could spend more on fertilizer, but my daughter's school fees are due, and the well pump is getting old. I always keep a few thousand yuan in reserve — a broken pump in July means no irrigation, and no irrigation means no crop. I'd rather apply slightly less fertilizer and sleep easy.
